output.reply: The evidence leans toward keeping positional. Cloud companies say running models is now a main reason they order accelerators, which is demand that recurs rather than a one-off training build, while a large cloud company moving more work to its own chips is a risk that plays out over quarters, not days. I would keep positional and not change the card.

findings.fact: Cloud companies said demand to run AI models, not only to train them, is now a main reason they order accelerators.
One large cloud company said it now runs more of its own AI work on chips it designs itself.
Ordering driven by running models is recurring demand, and a buyer shifting work to its own chips builds up over quarters; both fit a thesis measured in weeks to a few months rather than days.
